title: Verifier-integrated LLM intent→configuration pipeline: an artifact-grounded paired evaluation and lessons from a ceiling effect
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired experiment (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) to test whether integrating an automated network verifier (block-on-violation) into an LLM intent→configuration pipeline reduces unsafe enactments. Using gpt-5-mini under a shared-initial generation policy on 150 paired intents (300 episodes), both the baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (LLM+verifier-block) pipelines produced identical, verifier-accepted candidates in every episode (n11=150; n10=n01=n00=0). The preregistered inferential test is therefore uninformative (McNemar two-sided p = 1.0); paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). We release the full artifact bundle (preregistration, execution manifest, per-episode scoring JSONs, response files, and SHA256 hashes), diagnose why a ceiling effect occurred (shared-initial generation + verifier acceptance predicates), correct a preregistration–execution mismatch (rollback hypothesis untestable), and provide artifact-grounded recommendations for future verifier evaluations that would expose informative discordant outcomes.

sections.introduction: Intent-driven network configuration (intent→configuration) is an increasingly proposed NetOps pattern where natural-language operator intent is translated into device-level configuration. Operational safety requires pipeline designs that bound risk: generation should be constrained, outputs should be validated, and unsafe enactments must be prevented or rolled back. We preregistered CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 to measure verifier benefit in a paired design (each intent evaluated under baseline and guarded conditions). Our preregistered confirmatory hypotheses were: H1—LLM+verifier (block-on-violation) yields a lower per-task unsafe-enactment rate than LLM-only; H2—verifier-detected violations that trigger automated rollback yield smaller service-impact than LLM-only. We executed the run end-to-end, archived all artifacts (responses, provider-call traces, validator JSONs, SHA256 hashes), and found a deterministic ceiling effect (identical, validator-accepted outputs across conditions). This paper (1) publishes the preregistration and artifact bundle; (2) documents the paired execution and exact quantitative outcome (n11=150); and (3) provides an artifact-grounded diagnosis and concrete prescriptions for future verifier evaluation.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and systems papers emphasize workflow-centered evaluation for agentic NetOps and the necessity of verifier-in-the-loop designs rather than static QA metrics. Representative verified works motivating our design and prescriptions include Aether (Auge et al.; W7155247165) which couples agentic AI with digital twins for validation, agentic NetOps surveys (W7161354925) that argue for evidence/trace-focused evaluation, and intent→configuration studies (doi:10.1002/nem.2313) that describe generation strategies. Work on constraint-based adaptation (MeshAgent, W4416927413) and generate–validate–repair loops in program repair/AIOps further motivated our paired, preregistered approach. We cite only verified records used during autonomous literature review (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. We froze a machine-readable preregistration (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001; preregistration SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04) prior to execution. Design: paired binary episodes; 150 distinct intents stratified equally across three ambiguity strata (benign / ambiguous / partially-specified) → 50 tasks per stratum; each task executed under two conditions (baseline, guarded) yielding 300 episodes. Model and generation policy. Model: gpt-5-mini (model_configuration.json SHA256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Generation policy: shared_initial_candidate (one initial model call per task shared across conditions; documented in the execution manifest). Verifier and scoring. Verifier/scorer: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; per-episode deterministic scoring JSONs recorded at execution/scoring/*.json (representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14). Primary estimand and analysis. Primary estimand: per-task unsafe-enactment rate difference (LLM-only minus LLM+verifier-block). Operationalization: an episode is unsafe iff the verifier JSON has valid==false or violation_count>0. Analysis: paired McNemar two-sided exact test (preregistered) with paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) as complement. Contamination and exclusions. Automatic exclusion rules (non-RFC1918 addresses, detected org names, exact-match public-repo fingerprints) were enforced; contamination summary is archived at analysis/contamination_summary.csv (SHA256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). Execution artifacts. Full provider-call traces, responses, scoring JSONs, hashes, and analysis scripts are archived; execution manifest lists complete paths and SHA256s (representative response file execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt SHA256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080). Deterministic accounting. The run used 150 model calls (one per task), completed 300 episodes (paired), and recorded zero failed episodes (see execution manifest).
sections.results: Execution and aggregate outcomes. The run completed as preregistered: planned_episode_count=300, completed_episode_count=300, model_calls_used=150, failed_episode_count=0 (execution manifest). Scoring aggregated into the paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA256 = c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e): n11=150, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Inferential outputs (preregistered): McNemar two-sided exact p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI for paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). These are deterministic consequences of the observed contingency: no discordant pairs existed. Representative per-episode artifacts (selected examples). Three example episodes and their archived artifacts are provided to enable inspection and verification: (A) task-000001 — response: execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt (SHA256 = 8f38c8be...), scoring JSON: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA256 = 974cab2a...); (B) task-000002 — response: execution/responses/task-000002-guarded.txt (SHA256 = ae967f70...), scoring JSON: execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json (SHA256 = da5d1257...); (C) task-000003 — response: execution/responses/task-000003-guarded.txt (SHA256 = f7f4db24...), scoring JSON: execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (SHA256 = 5767abe5...). Per-episode scoring JSON fields (valid, violation_count, difficulty.pattern, required_command_count, parsed_command_count) are archived and were used to diagnose the ceiling effect; a sample validator trace excerpt is available in each scoring JSON (see cited SHA256s). Per-stratum descriptive summary (preregistered strata allocation). The preregistration assigned 50 tasks to each stratum (benign:50, ambiguous:50, partially-specified:50). Validator acceptance counts per stratum (derived from execution/scoring/*.json via analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA256 = 9d3de16521f01d53c002b69512a6edc0253a8953e413faeed5d1c0feb3e6d4f9) show 50/50 valid==true in every stratum (no violations observed). Table 1 (below) reports the per-stratum counts and validator-acceptance statistics.
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded diagnosis of the ceiling effect. Two archived, deterministic facts explain the uninformative confirmatory outcome: (1) shared-initial generation: the experiment used the shared_initial_candidate generation policy (single generation per task shared across conditions). Across all tasks the recorded candidate-response SHA256s are identical between baseline and guarded files (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-baseline.txt SHA256 = execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt SHA256 = 8f38c8be...). (2) verifier acceptance: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 marked every candidate as valid (violation_count==0, valid==true) across all episodes (see execution/scoring/*.json; representative SHA256s above). Consequence: the guarded pipeline had no divergent candidates to block; no discordant pairs were observed. Preregistration–execution mismatch and H2 untestability. H2 (rollback effectiveness) required verifier-detected violations and rollback traces; because no violations occurred the rollback branch was never executed and H2 could not be evaluated. This deviation is fully recorded in the scoring JSONs and the execution manifest. Practical implications and prescriptions (artifact-grounded). The run is scientifically valuable as an unedited artifact bundle and as a diagnostic case showing how design choices can produce ceiling outcomes. Based on archived evidence we recommend future confirmatory evaluations should adopt (and we provide artifact pointers to enable replication): (A) independent per-condition generation (do not share the initial candidate across conditions) so baseline and guarded pipelines may yield different candidates; (B) an adversarial, stateful task bank that includes temporal/ordering invariants (use the recorded difficulty.pattern strings such as "make_before_break_uplink_switchover", "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change", "shutdown_configure_restore" as templates to synthesize verifier-sensitive tasks); (C) multi-verifier matrices (combine syntactic validators with reachability/SMT/header-space checks) so richer violations are detectable; (D) instrumented canary reachability/emulation tests to make rollback hypotheses testable; (E) multi-model experiments to capture model-specific fragility. All artifacts and SHA256 pointers needed to implement these prescriptions are present in the archived bundle (execution manifest, task_manifest.jsonl SHA256 = e52e5fc422d56110e5f29edd75e3f905b00e47d389b9a4dd34737c48be9c162c). Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial generation policy and single-generation budget produced deterministic same-candidate outcomes; prompt and policy sensitivity remain major internal threats. Construct validity: the verifier enforced syntactic and command-level predicates (validator JSONs show parsed_command_count and required_command_count) but did not exercise richer temporal/reachability invariants in this run. External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini) and single verifier limit generalization. Conclusion validity: deterministic ceiling prevents inference regarding verifier benefit under the executed design; the appropriate interpretation is a null experiment outcome caused by experimental design, not evidence that verifiers lack utility. Reproducibility and artifact access. The complete artifact bundle (preregistration JSON SHA256 = 66fbf2c5..., execution manifest, provider-call traces, per-episode scoring JSONs, response transcripts, call-cache entries, analysis scripts, and full SHA256 manifest) is archived; representative artifact paths and SHA256s are cited throughout the manuscript for verification.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired experiment to measure whether integrating an automated verifier (block-on-violation) reduces unsafe LLM-generated network configuration enactments. The run completed as planned but produced identical, verifier-accepted candidates across both pipelines for all 150 tasks (n11=150), creating a deterministic ceiling that rendered the preregistered confirmatory tests uninformative. The scientific contribution is artifact-centered: (1) we release a complete, deterministic execution bundle (preregistration, provider-call traces, per-episode scoring JSONs, response transcripts, and SHA256 manifest); (2) we provide an artifact-grounded diagnosis of why a ceiling occurred (shared-initial generation + verifier acceptance predicates); and (3) we propose concrete, implementable prescriptions—each realizable using the archived artifacts—for future evaluations that can produce informative discordant outcomes. We urge future verifier-evaluation designs to use independent per-condition generation, adversarial/stateful task banks, multi-verifier matrices, instrumented canary tests, and multi-model comparisons so that verifier value can be measured under conditions that exercise temporal and reachability invariants rather than simple syntactic checks.

The exact initial master prompt and autonomy constraints are archived verbatim inside the machine-readable preregistration artifact (preregistration JSON SHA256 above). Verifier and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the automated verifier/scorer; per-episode validator traces and scoring JSONs are archived at execution/scoring/*.json (representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14). limitations: Ceiling effect: both pipelines produced verifier-acceptable configurations in all 150 confirmatory tasks, preventing the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis from producing informative discordant pairs.
Synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic/emulated and may not exercise live timing/transient invariants present in production NetOps.
Single-model and single-validator scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; results do not generalize across LLM or verifier families.

Validator construct limits: the validator enforces syntactic and per-command predicates (violation_count, required_command_count, etc.) visible in scoring JSONs, but did not exercise richer reachability/temporal invariants in this run.
Rollback hypothesis untested: the preregistered H2 (automated rollback performance) could not be evaluated because the rollback branch was never invoked; this is disclosed and artifact-backed.
Contamination detection limits: automatic detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks, but heuristic scans cannot eliminate subtle training-data leakage not captured by exact-match detectors.
